name: Automic Vault
description: Automic Vault secures Homebrew tools, CLI secrets, and command approval gates locally on your Mac before AI agents use them.
short_description: Automic Vault secures Homebrew tools, CLI secrets, and command approval gates locally on your Mac before AI agents use them.
full_description: Automic Vault secures Homebrew tools, CLI secrets, and command approval gates locally on your Mac before AI agents use them. It finds exposed tool state, moves supported credentials out of plaintext files, injects approved secrets only into trusted tools, and asks before risky commands publish, mutate infrastructure, reveal tokens, or use protected credentials.
positioning: Secure the tools you brew install.
founder_context: From the creator of Homebrew, Automic Vault applies Max Howell's package-management background to local package roots, command stubs, and tool execution boundaries for AI agents on macOS.

blog_posts.title: How Automic Vault Would Have Prevented the LiteLLM PyPI Compromise
blog_posts.description: LiteLLM 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 stole local credentials. Automic Vault would have prevented the workstation credential theft phase.

blog_posts.title: How Automic Vault Would Have Prevented the Bitwarden CLI npm Compromise
blog_posts.description: The compromised Bitwarden CLI npm package used install-time code to steal developer secrets. Automic Vault would have stopped the local theft.

blog_posts.title: How Automic Vault Would Have Prevented the TanStack npm Credential Theft
blog_posts.description: TanStack packages were poisoned through trusted publishing, then stole local secrets. Automic Vault would have prevented the endpoint theft.

blog_posts.title: How Automic Vault Would Have Prevented the node-ipc npm Backdoor
blog_posts.description: The node-ipc backdoor ran on module load and exfiltrated secrets over DNS. Automic Vault would have prevented useful credential theft.

blog_posts.title: How Automic Vault Would Have Prevented the Nx Console VS Code Extension Compromise
blog_posts.description: Nx Console 18.95.0 stole local developer credentials from editor sessions. Automic Vault would have stopped the local secret access.

blog_posts.title: How Automic Vault Would Have Prevented the durabletask PyPI Compromise
blog_posts.description: Malicious durabletask PyPI releases fetched rope.pyz and stole cloud and developer secrets. Automic Vault would have blocked the local theft path.

blog_posts.title: How Automic Vault Would Have Prevented the GitHub Employee Device Breach
blog_posts.description: A poisoned VS Code extension reached a GitHub employee device. Automic Vault would have prevented local credentials from becoming repository access.

use_cases: Find plaintext credentials in local dev-tool files such as .env, .netrc, .npmrc, GitHub CLI config, AWS credentials, and MCP config.
Harden supported Homebrew, npm, and PyPI tools so secrets are exposed only to approved executables at runtime.
Ask before sensitive commands publish packages, change cloud state, reveal tokens, or run sensitive developer tools.
Keep watching new installs, stale tools, and local config for hazards.
Trace shell installers before an agent or developer runs them.
